what: Jabbit hand review of ClinicalTrials.gov records on muscle during GLP-1 drug treatment
method: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 pulled 2026-10-19 16:07 EDT: every study listing semaglutide, tirzepatide, retatrutide, orforglipron or liraglutide as an intervention, plus free-text searches pairing GLP-1 drug names with sarcopenia/lean/muscle terms, with resistance training/creatine/protein/whey/leucine/HMB, with myostatin/activin and named muscle drugs, and with grip/physical function/gait/SPPB/frailty terms. Keyword-flagged records were read by hand. Kept: the study gives one of those drugs (or GLP-1 drugs as a class) and either names muscle, lean mass, strength or physical function as an aim or primary outcome, or adds a muscle drug, exercise, protein/nutrition or creatine and registers a muscle, lean-mass, strength or function outcome. Strength/function = a registered outcome naming grip, strength, chair stands, SPPB, gait or walk tests, stair climb, timed up-and-go, 1RM/leg press, balance or physical function/performance (questionnaires such as SF-36 not counted). Counts are a lower bound: a study that uses none of these words in its title, summary, arms or outcomes would be missed, and records that mention muscle only in secondary outcomes without a muscle aim were not counted.
